candidates.comment: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: parents
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their biological or adoptive parents. Also called is a child of, has as a parent, is parented by. Examples: John is a parent of Mary. Jane is a parent of David. The parents of a child are their mother and father. Distinct from children, which points from a parent to their offspring.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: parent
candidates.comment: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor. Examples: "Child A parent 'Parent B'", "Person X parent 'Mother Y'", "Person Z parent 'Father W'". Distinct from children, which describes the offspring.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their child. Also called "offspring", "son", "daughter". Examples: "John children Jane", "Mary children Peter". Distinct from parent, which indicates the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: performTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to execute instructions or a direction, excluding preparation time. Also called execution time, active time, task duration. Examples: A recipe's instructions have a perform time of 'PT30M'. A DIY project direction has a perform time of 'PT2H'. A workout routine has a perform time of 'PT45M'. Distinct from prepTime, which is the time to prepare supplies.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: byArtist
candidates.comment: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: actors
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: entertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An entertainment business relation between a perform action and the entertainment business where the action occurred. Also called "venue", "performance location", "showplace". Examples: "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Concert Hall'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Theater Royal'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Comedy Club'". Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any place an action occurs.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: partOfInvoice
candidates.comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: originatesFrom
candidates.comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: translationOfWork
candidates.comment: A translation of work relation between a creative work and the original work from which it was translated. Also called original work, source work, translated from. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Don Quixote (Spanish)' translationOfWork 'Don Quijote (original)'", "CreativeWork 'The Little Prince (English)' translationOfWork 'Le Petit Prince (French)'", "CreativeWork 'War and Peace (English)' translationOfWork 'Война и мир (Russian)'".

candidates.label: inDefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A defined term set inclusion relation between a defined term and the defined term set it belongs to. Also called part of term set, contained in term set, term set member. Examples: "A defined term is in a defined term set for medical conditions.", "The term is in a defined term set URL.", "This defined term belongs to a specific term set.". Distinct from hasDefinedTerm, which describes the inverse (set has term).

candidates.label: inCodeSet
candidates.comment: A code set inclusion relation between a category code and the category code set it belongs to. Also called part of code set, contained in code set, code set member. Examples: "A category code is in a code set for product types.", "The code is in a code set URL.", "This category code belongs to a specific code set.". Distinct from hasCategoryCode, which describes the inverse (set has code).

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: checkinTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a lodging business or reservation, indicating the earliest time for check-in. Also called "arrival time", "earliest check-in", "check-in starts". Examples: "Hotel lodging business checkinTime '15:00'", "Flight reservation checkinTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00'". Distinct from checkoutTime, which specifies the latest time for departure.

candidates.label: courseSchedule
candidates.comment: A temporal structure relation between a course instance and its length and pace. Also called: course timetable, class schedule, academic calendar. Examples: "Fall Semester Course" course schedule "Mondays and Wednesdays, 10:00-11:30 AM", "Intensive Workshop" course schedule "Full-day, 5 days", "Online Module" course schedule "Self-paced, complete within 8 weeks".

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: featureList
candidates.comment: A feature list relation between a software application and the functionalities or modules it provides. Also called: application features, software capabilities, module list. Examples: "Word Processor" feature list "Spell Check, Grammar Check, Document Templates", "Photo Editor" feature list "Layers, Filters, Cropping", "Operating System" feature list "Multitasking, File Management, User Accounts".

candidates.label: accessibilityFeature
candidates.comment: An accessibility feature relation between a creative work and its specific features designed to enhance accessibility. Also called accessible features, accessibility enhancements, content adaptations. Examples: "A movie's accessibility feature is 'captions'.", "An image's accessibility feature is 'altText'.", "A document's accessibility feature is 'highContrast'."

candidates.label: amenityFeature
candidates.comment: An amenity feature relation between an accommodation, floor plan, lodging business, or place and a characteristic or service it offers. Also called facility, service, characteristic, convenience. Examples: "A hotel room's amenity feature is 'free Wi-Fi'.", "The apartment's amenity feature is 'gym access'.", "A park's amenity feature is 'playground'."

candidates.label: contactOption
candidates.comment: A feature relation for a contact point, indicating an available option such as a toll-free number or accessibility support. Also called "contact feature", "available option", "support option". Examples: "Customer service contact point contactOption 'TollFree'", "Accessibility contact point contactOption 'HearingImpairedSupported'".

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: browserRequirements
candidates.comment: A description of browser requirements for a web application. Also called "browser compatibility", "required browser features". Examples: "Online banking app browserRequirements 'Requires Chrome 80+ or Firefox 75+'", "Video streaming service browserRequirements 'Supports HTML5 video and DRM'".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: lodgingUnitDescription
candidates.comment: A unit description relation between a lodging reservation and a full textual description of the lodging unit. Also called: room description, accommodation details, unit features. Examples: "Hotel Reservation lodgingUnitDescription 'King-size bed, ocean view, balcony'", "Apartment Rental lodgingUnitDescription 'Two bedrooms, fully equipped kitchen, city view'", "Cabin Booking lodgingUnitDescription 'Rustic cabin, fireplace, lake access'".

candidates.label: contactlessPayment
candidates.comment: A feature relation for a payment card, indicating whether it supports contactless payment technology. Also called "NFC payment", "tap to pay", "RFID payment". Examples: "Credit card contactlessPayment true", "Debit card contactlessPayment false".

candidates.label: reviewAspect
candidates.comment: The specific part, feature, or facet of an item that a review or rating pertains to. Also called review focus, aspect reviewed, rating dimension. Examples: `Restaurant Review` reviewAspect `"Service Quality"`, `Product Rating` reviewAspect `"Battery Life"`, `Movie Review` reviewAspect `"Acting Performance"`.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: acceptedAnswer
candidates.comment: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response. Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."
